prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck—what’s best depends on your case (severity, liability issues, insurance limits) and what you value (big-firm resources vs. individual attention, trial experience vs. quick settlement). I can help you find the right attorney for your situation. Meanwhile, here’s how to choose and what to do next.

Quick essentials
- Act quickly: Texas generally has a 2-year statute of limitations for personal injury claims (so don’t wait).
- Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover), but details differ—get it in writing.
- Verify credentials with the State Bar of Texas and look for board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if applicable).

How to find a good car-wreck lawyer in Houston
- Check: State Bar of Texas lawyer search, Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Google/ Yelp reviews, and local bar association referrals.
- Look for lawyers who focus on car wrecks/auto collisions and who have trial experience and resources to handle medical liens and large claims.
- Ask friends, family, or medical providers for referrals.

Key factors to consider
- Relevant experience and track record in auto accident cases (settlements and verdicts).
- Trial experience (most cases settle, but you want someone who will try the case if necessary).
- Who will handle the case day-to-day (the named partner or an associate/paralegal).
- Communication style and availability.
- Resources to advance litigation costs (experts, investigations).
- Fee and cost arrangement (contingency percentage, who pays costs if you lose).
- Local knowledge of Houston courts, judges, and insurers.

Questions to ask at a free consult
1. How long have you handled car wreck/personal injury claims?  
2. What percentage of your practice is car-crash cases?  
3. Who will handle my case day-to-day?  
4. What’s your trial experience and recent results in similar cases?  
5. How do you charge (contingency %)? What about out-of-pocket costs?  
6. How will medical bills and liens be handled?  
7. What’s a realistic range for my case and timeline to resolution?  
8. How often and by what method will you update me?  
9. Do you have references from past clients?  
10. Are you licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of Texas?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report or crash report number  
- Photos of the scene/vehicles/injuries  
- Medical records and bills (or names of treating providers)  
- Insurance information (your and the other driver’s)  
- Correspondence with insurers, if any  
- Witness names/contacts

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or outcome.  
- High-pressure “sign now” tactics.  
- Reluctance to put fee arrangements in writing or to answer simple questions about costs.  
- Poor communication or evasive answers about who will actually do the work.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list several Houston personal injury attorneys with strong reputations in auto cases (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood).  
- Draft an email/script for contacting lawyers or a list of attorneys to check (Super Lawyers, local AV-rated attorneys, etc.).  

Which would you prefer—tips to search yourself, or a short vetted list tailored to your Houston neighborhood?
